## Solution

The statement is **FALSE** in general. The correct limit is $\frac{t_n}{\log n} \to 0$, which equals $L$ only when $L=0$.

---

### Proof

We apply the **Stolz–Cesàro theorem** ($\infty/\infty$ form): if $(A_n)$ is strictly increasing with $A_n\to\infty$ and $\dfrac{B_n-B_{n-1}}{A_n-A_{n-1}}\to \ell$, then $\dfrac{B_n}{A_n}\to\ell$.

Set $B_n = t_n$ and $A_n = \log n$. Then $A_n$ is strictly increasing and $A_n\to\infty$, and
$$B_n - B_{n-1} = t_n - t_{n-1} = b_n, \qquad A_n - A_{n-1} = \log n - \log(n-1) = \log\!\left(\frac{n}{n-1}\right).$$

For large $n$,
$$\log\!\left(\frac{n}{n-1}\right) = -\log\!\left(1-\frac{1}{n}\right) = \frac{1}{n} + O\!\left(\frac{1}{n^2}\right) \sim \frac{1}{n}.$$

Therefore
$$\frac{B_n - B_{n-1}}{A_n - A_{n-1}} = \frac{b_n}{\log\!\left(\frac{n}{n-1}\right)} \sim \frac{b_n}{1/n} = n\,b_n = \frac{n\log n\cdot b_n}{\log n}.$$

By hypothesis $n\log n\cdot b_n \to L$, so
$$\frac{B_n - B_{n-1}}{A_n - A_{n-1}} \sim \frac{L}{\log n} \to 0.$$

By Stolz–Cesàro,
$$\boxed{\frac{t_n}{\log n} \to 0.}$$

This equals $L$ **only when $L=0$**, so the claimed statement $\frac{t_n}{\log n}\to L$ is **false** for any $L\neq 0$.

### Explicit Counterexample

Take $b_1=0$ and $b_n = \dfrac{1}{n\log n}$ for $n\geq 2$. Then
$$n\log n\cdot b_n = 1 \quad\text{for all } n\geq 2, \qquad\text{so } L=1.$$

The partial sums satisfy (by integral comparison)
$$t_n = \sum_{k=2}^{n}\frac{1}{k\log k} \sim \int_2^n \frac{dx}{x\log x} = \log\log n - \log\log 2 \sim \log\log n.$$

Hence
$$\frac{t_n}{\log n} \sim \frac{\log\log n}{\log n} \to 0 \neq 1 = L.$$

This confirms the statement fails when $L\neq 0$. $\blacksquare$
